name: Resveratrol

lead: Resveratrol is a polyphenol found in grape skins, berries and peanuts, popularized by the "French paradox" and by early sirtuin-activation research. It is sold as a supplement and used in some skincare products.

It is promoted for longevity and skin health. Human trials show small effects on some metabolic markers, but evidence for longevity or visible anti-aging is insufficient, and its poor bioavailability limits interpretation.

paras: Proposed mechanisms include activation of SIRT1 and AMPK and antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity. Some of the sirtuin findings have been disputed, and oral resveratrol is rapidly metabolized, leaving little free compound in circulation.
Usually well tolerated; high doses can cause gastrointestinal upset. It may interact with anticoagulants and drugs metabolized by CYP enzymes. Legal as a supplement; product quality varies.
